name: Ruth
bio:
Ruth is a Moabite woman whose loyalty and faith give the book its name, even though she was born outside Israel. After marrying Naomi's son Mahlon and then losing him to death along with her father-in-law and brother-in-law, Ruth has every reason to return to her own people and gods, as her sister-in-law Orpah does. Instead she makes one of the most quoted vows of devotion in Scripture — "Whither thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God" (1:16) — choosing to leave her homeland and bind her future to Naomi and to the God of Israel.

In Bethlehem, Ruth works to support them both, gleaning leftover grain in the fields — hard, humble labor reserved for the poor — and happens to glean in a field belonging to Boaz, a relative of Naomi's late husband. Boaz notices her diligence and her reputation for kindness to Naomi, and shows her favor. Following Naomi's guidance, Ruth approaches Boaz at the threshing floor at night and asks him, as a near kinsman, to extend his protection over her — a bold but respectful request for him to act as kinsman-redeemer. Boaz agrees to secure the right to redeem Elimelech's family line, marries Ruth, and they have a son, Obed. Through this marriage, a Moabite widow becomes the great-grandmother of King David and is named in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew 1 — her story standing as a picture of steadfast loyalty (the Hebrew hesed) and of God's welcome extended even to outsiders.
